newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels close in on Kikwit town - residents.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels close in on Kikwit town - residents.

text.p: Rebels advancing on Zaire's capital Kinshasa were closing in on the provincial town of Kikwit on Monday and local authorities asked government soldiers to lay down their arms, residents said.

"Kikwit is on the point of falling. There is no panic and people are calm," said a resident in radio contact with Kinshasa, 400 km (250 miles) to the west. Residents said rebels had not yet entered the town.

They said the local administrator had asked the contingent of Zairean troops to lay down their arms and cease any resistance against Laurent Kabila's rebels, who have captured more than half of Zaire's vast territory since last October.
A senior military official in the capital said he was unable to confirm or deny the report.

Kikwit, which shot into world limelight because of an ebola virus epidemic which killed more than 120 people there in 1995, is the commercal capital the Bandundu province that supplies most of Kinshasa's domestically produced food.
